Version history
===============

v1.0.0  The first build confirmed working in game.
        Radius 30 sphere, 8,486 blocks placed in 3.6 real seconds, held for 120s of real
        time, restored in 0.45s. Bright blue textures, no title cards.

v1.1.0  Everything requested after that:
          - abyssal palette: near-black wall (13,14,18), deep teal floor (22,58,64)
          - title cards: the domain name, then its epithet with corner brackets, in blue
          - thrown spells curve towards whatever is trapped inside
          - lock-on auto-targeting, OFF by default (see DomainConfig.AUTO_TARGET_ENABLED)
          - scroll lists the effects with the levels they run at
          - Overflow and Rainfall run one level above the domain, wet amplifiers included
          - mana cost 1000 / 2000 / 3000 instead of 200 / 400 / 600

v1.2.0  The cast animation, and the mana cost verified.
          - a 1.5 second wind-up: the hands draw together over 1.0s, hold still for 0.5s, and
            the last of the gap closes in 0.4s as the sphere appears
          - CastType LONG with the cast time pinned, so the animation cannot be cut short by
            cast-time-reduction gear
          - two authored player animations, domain_seal and domain_seal_finish, because none
            of Iron's 75 fits: they either snap the hands into place or are a charging tremor

Getting the seal right took four attempts, and the two things that were wrong are worth
knowing if it is ever touched again:

  - Minecraft applies a model part's rotation as X, then Y, then Z. X swings an arm forward
    (-90 is straight ahead), and Y is what opens and closes a pair of forward-pointing hands.
    Z only swings a *hanging* arm sideways, so animating it while X is near -90 spins the arm
    in place instead of moving it - which is what the first attempts looked like.
  - The sign is counter-intuitive: for the right arm a *larger* negative Y is further inward.
    Seeing the hands spread during a wind-up that was meant to close them means the Y values
    need their magnitudes swapped, not their signs flipped.

Rolling back
============

  git clone https://github.com/taccx/mc.git
  cd mc
  git checkout v1.2.0        # or v1.1.0, v1.0.0

The jar is NOT byte-reproducible: build.gradle writes an Implementation-Timestamp into the
manifest, so rebuilding the same source produces a jar differing by a byte or two. Compare
behaviour, not hashes, when checking out an older tag and rebuilding.

Installing
==========

Copy the jar into the modpack's mods folder while the game is CLOSED:
  ...\.minecraft\versions\娑熸吉涔嬬瘒路濡傛稛婕箣鎵€瑙乗mods\

Replacing it while the game is loading corrupts the mod scan and crashes the game with a
misleading UnionFileSystem$NoSuchFileException. install-jar.ps1 checks this and refuses.
